curriculum: The English-taught 2026-entry degree totals 180 EC. The 135 EC major has eight first-year courses (60), three required methods courses (22.5), a thematic package (22.5), two advanced selections (15) and the thesis (15). The 45 EC profile is elective within faculty rules. Article 3.5.1 gives 90 EC for Annex 1 taught requirements, which conflicts with its enumerated courses, the 135 EC major cap in the same article, and the cohort-specific student curriculum. Annex 1 explicitly applies to this cohort, supplies 60 plus 22.5, and is independently corroborated by the detailed 2026-entry curriculum. That interpretation accounts for all 135 EC without fabricating an extra component. Annex 6 preserves older-cohort requirements separately. The selected welfare package and advanced philosophy and history choices follow official order. The advanced history title and the third methods title are provisional, so no unsupported content or exact equivalence is attributed to them.
progression: The eight first-year courses precede the year-two methods and thematic work. Integrating Insights, Knowledge and Reasoning, both advanced electives and the thesis provide 45 advanced EC in the major. Year two contributes 30 advanced EC before the thesis. The current thesis catalogue requires programme enrollment and 15 advanced EC, and the thesis integrates two disciplines. Year three includes a thesis lab and final thesis together worth 15 EC; 45 elective EC includes at least 15 intermediate EC under the faculty EER. The programme page identifies 45 of 60 first-year EC for positive binding study advice. No assumed first-year elective, older skills course or extra thesis credit is inserted.
